name: DGSAT I (Hubble)
blurb: DGSAT I, an ultra-diffuse galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: dgsati-hubble
story: DGSAT I spreads as wide as a giant galaxy yet glows as faintly as a dwarf, and it sits far from any crowd. Hubble counted its globular clusters to weigh the unseen dark matter around it.

claims.text: DGSAT I is an isolated, quiescent ultra-diffuse galaxy
Ultra-diffuse galaxies have dwarf-like luminosities but giant-like sizes
DGSAT I lies in a much sparser environment than similar galaxies in the Coma and Virgo clusters
Hubble ACS imaging was used to count its globular clusters, as a proxy for its dark matter halo mass
Hubble imaging found its globular clusters and a high cluster mass fraction consistent with an overmassive dark matter halo
